title: Treble — the workhorse of UK crochet
subtitle: Three loops, two-stage finish, the granny square and most blanket patterns in one stitch
excerpt: Treble is the most-used stitch in UK crochet. It builds granny squares, blankets, and garment bodies. The two-stage pull-through and the ch-3 turning chain are where most beginners stumble — this tutorial walks both in full.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776 — the long treble as the standard pattern stitch. Weldon's Practical Crochet, Vol. 1 (1886) — treble stitch in flat patterns and in the round.

glossaryTerms.definition: UK term for the standard tall crochet stitch: yarn over before inserting, pull up a loop (three loops on hook), yarn over pull through two, yarn over pull through remaining two. US patterns call this double crochet.
Multiple trebles worked into the same stitch and joined at the top into one. The foundation of granny squares and many motif patterns.

content.text: is the UK's default pattern stitch — most British crochet patterns that say 'work treble across' mean this. One yarn-over before inserting, three loops on the hook after pulling up, then two yarn-overs to close the stitch in pairs. The height is roughly three times a chain link. US patterns call the same move double crochet (dc).

attrs.title: The critical UK/US split
attrs.body: UK 'treble' (tr) equals US 'double crochet' (dc). If you follow UK patterns, UK 'treble' is the stitch you work most often. If you follow US patterns, the same move appears as 'double crochet'. The standard granny square, worked from a UK pattern, calls for treble clusters. From a US pattern, those same clusters are called double crochet clusters.

content.text: Chain 14. The treble turning chain is ch 3, which counts as the first treble.
Row 1: ch 3 (counts as first treble). Yarn over, then insert hook into the 4th chain from the hook.
Yarn over and pull up a loop — three loops on the hook.
Yarn over and pull through the first two loops — two loops remain.
Yarn over and pull through the remaining two loops. One treble made.
Work 1 tr in each chain across — 12 tr in total including the ch-3. Turn.
Row 2: ch 3 (counts as first tr). Skip the first stitch below the ch-3. Work 1 tr in each of the next 10 stitches. Work 1 tr into the top of the ch-3 from the previous row. 12 tr. Turn.

are several trebles worked into the same stitch or space but joined at the top into one. To make a 3tr cluster: work each of the three trebles to the last yarn-over (leaving two loops each time), then yarn over and pull through all four loops at once. The cluster forms a closed dome. Granny squares are built from 3tr clusters worked into chain spaces.

items.symptom: Work gets wider row by row
items.cause: Working into the ch-3 turning chain at the end of each return row as an extra stitch, rather than treating it as the first stitch
items.fix: The ch-3 stands in for the first treble. At the end of each row, the last treble goes into the top of the ch-3 from the row below — it replaces a stitch, not adds to it.

items.symptom: A visible hole between the ch-3 and the first treble
items.cause: Skipping the first stitch and then leaving a gap before the second
items.fix: Place a stitch marker in the 2nd stitch (the first one to work into) at the start of each new row. The ch-3 counts as stitch 1; your first hook insertion goes into stitch 2.

items.cause: Pulling the working yarn too far after the first yarn-over, losing one of the three loops
items.fix: Keep all three loops on the hook clearly visible before the first yarn-over close. Check the loop count at each step — three loops before first close, two loops before second close.

content.text: The granny cluster tutorial is the direct application — three trebles into a chain space, worked in the round. The V-stitch and shell stitch both use trebles grouped differently for lacy openwork. Front and back post treble stitches work around the post of the treble rather than into the top loops for raised Aran-style panels.
